title: Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam, Varanasi
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Saral Srivastava, J.; Sudhanshu Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Executive Engineer to decide a fresh representation in accordance with law.
headnote: Where a Clause 6.5 objection to a disconnection memo and a claim for one bill on the meter's final reading remain pending, the High Court will not decide the billing dispute on merits. The consumer may file a fresh representation before the Executive Engineer, who shall decide it in accordance with law after notice and hearing.
facts: Parvati Devi obtained a 7.5 HP connection from PuVVNL on 15 July 2017. The meter showed no current, so no bills issued. After her complaint the meter was changed on 23 January 2021, still without a reading. On 21 March 2025 the licensee disconnected on a recorded 4468 KWH and arrears of Rs 4,23,419. She objected under Clause 6.5 on 1 November 2025 seeking restoration and a single bill on that final reading; the objection remained pending when she approached the High Court.

holding_units.holding: A writ seeking a single bill from inception on the meter's final reading, while a Clause 6.5 objection to disconnection and arrears remains pending, is disposed without examining merits; the consumer may submit a fresh representation to the Executive Engineer, who shall consider and decide it strictly in accordance with law after notice and opportunity of hearing.

not_decided.point: Whether one bill from inception is due on the final reading of 4468 KWH, and whether disconnection and arrears of Rs 4,23,419 are sustainable
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to go into merits; Executive Engineer to decide the representation in accordance with law.
